problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Shipment Alpha: size 69 cubic meters
* Shipment Beta: size 70 cubic meters
* Shipment Gamma: size 63 cubic meters
* Shipment Delta: size 70 cubic meters
* Shipment Epsilon: size 50 cubic meters
* Shipment Zeta: size 63 cubic meters
* Shipment Eta: size 43 cubic meters
* Shipment Theta: size 38 cubic meters
* Shipment Iota: size 69 cubic meters
* Shipment Kappa: size 49 cubic meters
* Shipment Lambda: size 65 cubic meters
* Shipment Mu: size 48 cubic meters
* Shipment Nu: size 55 cubic meters
* Shipment Xi: size 68 cubic meters
* Shipment Omicron: size 63 cubic meters
* Shipment Pi: size 33 cubic meters
* Shipment Rho: size 59 cubic meters
* Shipment Sigma: size 66 cubic meters
* Shipment Tau: size 66 cubic meters
* Shipment Upsilon: size 45 cubic meters
* Shipment Phi: size 55 cubic meters
* Shipment Chi: size 46 cubic meters
* Shipment Psi: size 65 cubic meters
* Shipment Omega: size 49 cubic meters
* Shipment Aster: size 37 cubic meters
* Shipment Prime: size 50 cubic meters
* Shipment Double: size 66 cubic meters
* Shipment Triple: size 46 cubic meters
* Shipment Quad: size 62 cubic meters
* Shipment Star: size 47 cubic meters
* Shipment Dash: size 58 cubic meters
* Shipment Tilde: size 58 cubic meters

Each cargo plane has a maximum capacity of 100 cubic meters. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes possible. Every shipment must be placed on exactly one plane, and the total volume on any plane cannot exceed its capacity limit.
